intro: PowerPoint to PDF converts PPT, PPTX and PPS presentations into a PDF with one slide per page. It is the easiest way to send slides to a client, publish the ones from a lecture or print them, without depending on which PowerPoint version each person has or on fonts changing when the file is opened on another computer.

LibreOffice Impress does the conversion on our server, with no internet access. The text, shapes, tables, charts and images of every slide go into the PDF; animations, transitions and videos do not, because a PDF is static, so you see the final state of each slide.

Under more options you decide whether hidden slides, which are skipped by default, are included, and whether the speaker notes pages are added, handy as a script or as handouts. You also choose PDF, PDF/A-2b or PDF/UA, the JPEG quality and maximum resolution of photos (lower the resolution if the deck has many pictures and you want a light PDF) and the opening password if the file is protected.
The Pages field is applied to the finished PDF: type "1-10" to keep the first ten slides or "odd" for every other one. Several presentations at once give one PDF per file and a ZIP with all of them.
steps: Upload one or more PPT, PPTX or PPS presentations.
Say whether you want hidden slides or the speaker notes.
Download the PDF or the ZIP with all of them.

faq.q: Can I print several slides per sheet?
faq.a: Convert the presentation first and then run the PDF through Multiple pages per sheet, which puts 2, 4 or more slides on each sheet.
For ODP files there is ODP to PDF, with the same options.
